rulings.verbatim: Mac is the prove-and-build substrate. Full stop. NO paid infra without explicit founder sign-off. Free tier only (Oracle Always Free, GitHub-hosted runners, etc.). If it costs >EUR 0, it waits until after prove-and-build is done. Real cluster follows proof, never precedes it. Exceptions: none until further notice.
rulings.meaning: This laptop IS the production substrate until the founder says otherwise. Zero-cost only: GitHub-hosted runners, free tiers, and local clusters (k3d/k3s on this machine). Any proposal for a paid resource -- a rented node, a managed cluster, a paid tier, a provider invoice -- is REFUSED with 'Founder ruling R14: Mac substrate only', not escalated and not re-explained. A session that has already asked does not ask again in different words. PROOF COMES FIRST AND THE CLUSTER FOLLOWS IT: manifests, policies and drills are proved locally, and only a completed proof can justify reopening the spend question. Reverses the standing shape of crew#78, which was asking for a rented box before anything had ever been applied to a cluster.
rulings.enforced_by: rule-guard.py PreToolUse refuses a command that provisions or pays for infrastructure (hcloud/doctl/aws/gcloud/az create, fly deploy, terraform apply against a paid provider); crew#78 is marked blocked on this ruling so the ask stops regenerating

rulings.verbatim: first of all the macbook must never sleep, we need to prove everything works locally first, we dont want local to diverge from prod, no ruling stays everything working in laptop first
rulings.meaning: TWO PARTS, both binding. (1) THE MACBOOK NEVER SLEEPS. Under R14 this laptop IS production, so a sleep is a production outage, not a power setting. It is enforced by the OS itself -- 'sudo pmset -c sleep 0 disksleep 0 standby 0 powernap 0' -- and never by a caffeinate process under a KeepAlive LaunchAgent. caffeinate is a userland assertion: it is a no-op for system sleep on battery, it dies with the login session, and it is exactly the hand-rolled wrapper over a real OS setting that R6 bans. Measured 2026-08-24: com.founder.estate-awake reported PID alive and LastExitStatus 0 while the machine entered sleep 6 times on AC power that same morning. A session that finds a sleep in 'pmset -g log' treats it as an incident and routes it, with that log line as the receipt. The machine being on battery is the same outage arriving later; say so the moment you see it. (2) LOCAL IS THE REFERENCE, AND IT MUST NOT DIVERGE. Everything is proved working on this laptop before it is claimed anywhere else. There is no 'works in CI' and no 'works on the remote' -- a component that only runs after a manual step, only runs in a workflow, or only runs on a box that is not this one has not been proved. When local and any other environment disagree, that gap is the defect and the local side is the reference. This sharpens R14: R14 said the Mac is the substrate; R15 says a divergence from it is a bug you fix, not a difference you document.

rulings.verbatim: Command guards are Rego under policy/. Python guards are deprecated and rejected by CI.
rulings.meaning: A refusal that can be decided from the command string is an entry in policy/command.rego with its `re`, `marker`, `msg` and the `must_match`/`must_not_match` examples that keep it honest. `make guard NAME=x` scaffolds one and the test fails until real examples replace the TODOs. Do not add a `def rule_` to rule-guard.py: the count is ratcheted and CI refuses a rise. The six that remain shell out to git or gh to ask about the live tree, which Rego cannot do; they are the backlog, not the pattern. Numbered R16 because R15 was taken by the laptop-never-sleeps ruling while this branch was open. Enacted by the cutover in PR #28, which moved nine refusals after replaying 35,705 commands through both implementations with zero disagreements.
rulings.enforced_by: policy/hand_rolled_policy.rego (rule_ceiling, policy_dir_py, legacy line ceilings), gated by .github/workflows/policy.yml

rulings.verbatim: ok good job but alway research, it pays off all the tine
rulings.meaning: Before choosing any tool, standard, protocol or version, search the current state of the world and cite what you read. Not memory, not what the training data believed, not what another session asserted. The incident that paid for it: on 2026-08-24 a session started building an ingress on Traefik's own Docker labels. Research showed two things it did not know -- Kubernetes SIG Network retired the ingress-nginx controller on 2026-03-24, and Gateway API core is GA at v1.6.0 with 16 conformant implementations. The real decision was the config language, not the vendor: routes written as HTTPRoute are portable, routes written as vendor labels are not. Research changed the answer, and it cost one search. This is LAW 43 with a due date: the research is online, it is the agent's job, and it goes on the record with the sources named.
rulings.enforced_by: idp and crew: every ADR carries a Sources section with dated URLs; adr-sources-guard.py refuses a decision record that cites nothing

rulings.verbatim: also we have oracle free tier now, so we are ready, but firt we need to verify local env and prepare for the big one, add topersistent board notes or anywhere agets will refresh asap
rulings.meaning:
An Oracle Cloud Always Free tenancy now exists. It is the destination for the k8s migration (crew#78). It does not conflict with R14 zero-cost (free tier is free; R14 blocked PAID infra) nor R1 (Fly-specific).

STEP 1 IS A PROOF, NOT A COMPLAINT. 'Verify local env' means: run the WHOLE workload on the current substrate -- compose estate + k3d + Dagster + all 40 schedules -- and prove every part RECONCILES CORRECTLY. Reconciles means converges to desired state. Slow is a measurement; wrong is a failure. The proof requires everything UP at once, so stopping a component to make the machine comfortable destroys the proof rather than advancing it.

THE ARGUMENT THIS BUYS, AND THE ONE IT FORBIDS. With the proof in hand the Oracle case is 'the Mac cannot SCALE' -- correct behaviour, measured cost, headroom exhausted. Without it the only available case is 'the Mac is broken', which is a weak argument that reads as an operator who cannot run their own machine, and which a buyer's engineer takes apart in one sitting. Never argue the migration from breakage, throttling or an outage. Argue it from a green proof plus a ceiling.

ORDER: (1) prove the full workload reconciles, (2) prepare, (3) move. Nobody provisions Oracle capacity, creates a cluster or points anything at it until step 1 is proved with commands. 'We are ready' means the BLOCKER is gone, not start cutting over. R15 stands: the laptop is the substrate until the migration actually happens.
rulings.enforced_by: none yet -- procedural. Recorded on crew#78 as the premise change.
rulings.verbatim_followup: "Local green" does not mean "add more to the Mac." It means "prove the compose estate + k3d + Dagster + 40 schedules all reconcile correctly on the current substrate." Once that proof is in, the case for Oracle is that the Mac cannot scale, not that it is broken.

rulings.verbatim: Every container image in the estate must support both linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. No exceptions. No per-environment hacks. One image tag, two architectures, runtime picks automatically.
rulings.meaning: Every image the estate pushes is a single tag carrying a linux/amd64 and a linux/arm64 manifest, built by `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64` in GitHub Actions and pushed to GHCR. The Mac (x86_64) pulls amd64, OKE (Ampere) pulls arm64, nobody configures anything. Local builds go through idp/bin/build-image; CI blocks a single-arch push.
rulings.enforced_by: idp/bin/build-image (refuses a single --platform), idp/bin/multiarch-gate (every build-push-action and docker build call must name both platforms; fixtures both ways in idp-ci), idp/.github/workflows/build-multiarch.yml, STANDARDS.md row.

rulings.verbatim: we need this operational estate wide plain ... Every PR must update the BDD scenario or the auto-gen script. If the PR changes code but not the executable spec, the CI blocks merge. No manual doc updates. No 'I'll update the wiki later.' ... alert peers
rulings.meaning: Documentation that lives outside the execution path rots. Three mechanisms are the estate rule: (1) BDD scenarios are the spec and the test, so a PR that changes code must also change a .feature file or the generator that produces the live diagram; CI blocks it otherwise. (2) Diagrams are generated from live state (launchd, docker, the catalog), never drawn by hand. rulings.verbatim: you need to be clear and make things easy and intuitive, i miss too many things i need to do, if something depends on me and is blocking, it needs to be loud, visible and super friction free for me to act, law
rulings.meaning: When a step depends on the founder (a sign-in, an approval, a decision), the session (1) sends a PushNotification the moment it blocks, (2) states in the reply, above the fold, one line starting FOUNDER ACTION: with the exact URL, button or word he must give and where the tab is, (3) leaves nothing else for him to read or find. Never bury the ask under evidence, never pipe the prompt's URL into a log he cannot see, never say 'the tab should be open'. A blocked ask he did not see is the session's failure, not his.

rulings.verbatim: Stop thinking about prospector. Prospector is one customer. I want the research engine that prospector calls. The engine is the platform. Prospector is just a user.
rulings.meaning: The capability is an autonomous research engine. Five behaviours are proved before any scheduler, tracker or eval tool is touched: (1) question generation: 100 dossiers in, 10 unasked hypotheses out; (2) experiment design from one hypothesis: test, data, method; (3) execution and recording with no human; (4) calibration: Brier score against outcomes, published; (5) explanation: what it learned and why it changed its mind, one sentence. Tool choice is the cheapest that lets the five run; cost is optimised after. Sharpens R28.

rulings.verbatim: why are we concerned with the old dossiers when we want to exponentially improve things, old dossiers were duck taped together, our new capabilities should be sneering at this and want to prove they can generate much better ideas for all scales
rulings.meaning: The research engine is not fed, tuned to, or measured against the old prospector dossiers. It generates its own ideas from scratch, at every scale (one company, one market, the estate). The old corpus has one use: a baseline the engine must beat, shown side by side. Any plan whose first step is 'load the old dossiers' is the old system wearing a new name. Sharpens R31.

rulings.verbatim: ok lets adopt this but every 30 minutes not 4 hours ... and ensure everyone is permanently doing this without me asking ... this way even if agent sessions die, we can recover easily
rulings.meaning: Every session appends a handoff to ~/.estate/feed.md at least every 30 minutes: six lines at most, each starting with 🔴 Blocked / 🟡 Active / 🟢 Done / ⚪ Pending / 📍 State. The feed is the persistent brain; a session that dies has left its state there. A session that starts with 'Status' reads the feed and summarises it; nobody re-explains and the founder is never asked what the feed already says. Enforced by ~/.claude/scripts/feed-guard.py on Stop (blocks an overdue turn), SessionStart (injects the last entries) and UserPromptSubmit (reminder). Append with: python3 ~/.claude/scripts/feed-guard.py append --session <id> --lane <repo>.

rulings.verbatim: We are changing our approach entirely. ... we are officially banning the words "refactor," "rewrite," or "update" regarding the engine. ... every claim carries its source in an append-only, object-locked bucket ... every forecast is Brier-scored ... a Golden Corpus of 50-100 hand-researched dossiers is the oracle.
rulings.meaning: The research engine is net-new, not a cleanup of the old one. Every claim names a locked source (R2 object lock, append-only); every forecast is logged and Brier-scored (MLflow); the science plane is Argo/MLflow/Kubernetes; differential replay against the old engine is dead; a 50-100 item Golden Corpus, crew-researched online from existing dossier titles, is the oracle; the buyer sees a calibration curve. Full text: crew docs/rulings/R34-net-new-research-paradigm-verifiable-calibrated.md.

rulings.meaning: The research/science/ML capability is a platform layer in idp, on the same row as model routing and traces. rulings.verbatim: Research is a crew. Science/ML is a layer. ... Research discovers what to build. Science predicts when it will be ready, if it will break, and whether the founder can be interrupted. Both are mandatory. Neither can wait. ... a Python 'tapeworm' script writing to a local SQLite database on your Mac is completely incompatible with the elite, cloud-agnostic standard we just established. ... it must be impossible for any potential data point to be missed.
rulings.meaning: Research looks outward (markets, competitors, capabilities) and is a crew whose adoption decisions end with the founder's last call. Science/ML looks inward (sessions, CI, guards, budget, founder response) and is an embedded layer, always on, no opt-out: OTel Collector on the cluster, ClickHouse, MLflow + Langfuse, Brier-graded predictions, founder as calibration authority.
